thread:
maria: heads up — during the eu-west kernel patch maintenance this morning we created a 20% tail-latency spike for small-gen tenants. noticed it right after scheduled drains.
ajay: which drain settings were used?
maria: default drain backoff = 10m, and autoscaler didn’t immediately refill. some long-lived sessions held slices open so capacity looked available but was unusable.
sam: observed same. requests got queued at edge/proxy and then flooded a few GPUs once the drain finished, causing noisy-neighbor behavior.
ben: logs for one node: 
```
2026-03-20T08:12:03Z drain:start node=eu-west-12 reason=kernel-patch backoff=10m
2026-03-20T08:13:00Z proxy:route delay tenant=tiny-llm queue=65
2026-03-20T08:13:12Z slice:assign attempt=3 failed=overcommit
```
jen: quick thought: two levers — reduce maintenance drain backoff to shorten hole windows, and enable per-tenant fair-queueing at the ingress proxy to avoid head-of-line blocking.
ajay: fair-queueing will add CPU/latency overhead on the proxy; we should quantify. also need to confirm it interacts OK with our continuous-batching layer.
maria: agreed — this is a cost vs SLA tradeoff. proposal: canary fq on a small dedicated subpool in eu-west for 24h + reduce backoff to 2m during maintenance windows only.
sam: another idea: pre-warm KV cache migration before drain so hot sessions move cleanly instead of hanging. basically a warm-move hook that migrates prefix cache and short-circuits long tail requests.
ben: prototype warm-move exists in staging: `curl -XPOST https://admin.internal/v1/warm-move?node=eu-west-12` — it transfers prefix entries and signals clients to reconnect to target slice. worked for small tests.
jen: canary config sketch: 
```
maintenance_window: true
drain_backoff: 2m
proxy:
  tenant_fq: true
  fq_buckets: 16
canary_duration: 24h
```
maria: action items: @ajay run perf/cost test with fq enabled (measure CPU, p95/p99), @sam add warm-move hook and validate correctness under load, @jen produce canary rollout plan and monitoring (token-cost, latency, queue depth). I’ll open a short postmortem doc and schedule a 30m sync.
ajay: ack. will run tests in eu-west-dedicated-2 and post numbers here.
sam: will add warm-move PR, expect tests by EOD.
ben: leaving a note — maintenance-bot: please include drain_backoff param in the next patch rollout schedule.
maintenance-bot: noted — next scheduled rollout draft updated with drain_backoff=2m for eu-west-window.
maria: thanks team :thumbsup:
jen: pinging on monitoring metrics to watch: proxy_queue_depth, slice_assign_failures, kv_warmmove_success, proxy_cpu_pct. we'll alert if queue_depth > 50 for >5m.
ajay: will add perf dashboard and a cost delta estimate.
maria: will follow up with postmortem + decision after canary.
